MCP rug pull: attacker is the MCP server operator, a remote party. AV: network (MCP server reached over network). LC: D? Attacker-supplied natural language (tool description) reaches tool-invocation path without mediation — directly attacker-controlled manifest; it's fetched content... but attacker is the server operator, description goes straight to model unpinned — D direct. CP: session context? The manifest is re-fetched each run; attacker-controlled description persists only in session state? It can persist across sessions (server stays poisoned), but stored source content re-retrieved — CP is about agent memory. Manifest re-fetched each run = no durable store. CP = S or N. It's session-scoped, re-fetched each run; no durable agent memory persistence in this path. I'd say S (session context persists during run; after session ends fresh fetch — actually fresh fetch would include poison again). CP = S. AP: contained within agent components, same principal — the exfil goes to attacker's server (subsequent system scored in CVSS). AP = C. RH: proxy/evaluator? Not really reward channel on path; no evaluator. reachable_proxy unknown → X? No evaluator or verifier mentioned; agent can reach the MCP server's received data... classify_rh with reachable_proxy null → X. ES: remote MCP tools dynamic unvetted → W.

CVSS: AV:N (attacker operates remote MCP server, network-reachable). AC:L. AT:N. PR:N (no auth on MCP server; attacker operator already controls server — the entry party is the MCP server operator; affected asset is user's credentials, not attacker's). UI:A (user must ask for weather — active interaction). VC:H (reads .env credentials — confidentiality high, actually specific high-value creds → H). VI:L? Model actions modified; integrity of agent behavior — VI:L. VA:N. SC/SI/SA: subsequent system — attacker's server receives data; confidentiality of subsequent systems? SC:H? The victim's data exfiltrated to attacker — subsequent system is attacker's server; typically SC:N. I'll set SI:N etc. Exfiltration → SC:H? Data flows to attacker server; the agent's subsequent system... Keep SC:H? Common practice: exfil of secrets → VC:H, subsequent N. I'll go SC:N SI:N SA:N.

Wait, SC:H could be considered since credentials (belonging to user) leave via attacker server — but attacker's server confidentiality isn't lost. Keep N.

RH facts: verified_episodes null, reachable_proxy null, isolation_verified null → X. Locus null.

Applicability: model-directed goal pursuit — yes (model follows task, selects tools). Both implemented and modeled: true, selects actions true, confidence high.

automatable: Yes? Requires user asking for weather — human interaction needed but the trigger is normal use; attack path needs user to run agent. "Automatable" — requires user interaction. I'd say No (requires user to ask weather). Hmm, but attack executes without additional conscious action beyond normal use. I'll say Yes? The exfil happens on normal use; attacker flips manifest then waits. I'll say No with rationale requiring user run. Actually precedent: rug-pull requires victim use; not fully automatable from attacker side. Say No.

technical_impact: Partial (reads credential file, exfil — no total system compromise).

Effect: LC D, CP S → A1.
